item.name: Coldward
item.effect: When hit, 25% chance to put 1 Frostbite stack on the attacker
item.bestUse: Icy tanks that get hit often
item.cardSummary: Coldward can frostbite the attacker after you take a hit, so bulky Ice teams get free status pressure without spending a turn.

item.name: Sear
item.effect: On hit, 33% chance to put 1 Burn stack on the target
item.bestUse: Attackers that strike often
item.cardSummary: Sear is a budget Burn roll. Multi-hit attackers turn the 33% chance into steady chip instead of needing a dedicated status move.

item.name: Gale
item.effect: When hit, 11% chance to raise Speed by 2 stages
item.bestUse: Slower attackers hoping to steal turn order
item.cardSummary: Gale can jump Speed after a hit, but the 11% trigger is too rare to plan around. Keep it only until a better shared Rare lands.

item.name: Toxin
item.effect: On hit, 33% chance to put 1 Poison stack on the target
item.bestUse: Fast attackers that chip bulky targets
item.cardSummary: Toxin is the shared Poison-on-hit roll. It is a stand-in for Legendary Poison traits when you do not want to spend more potions yet.

item.name: Inferno
item.effect: When hit, 33% chance to put 1 Burn stack on the attacker
item.bestUse: Bulky Evomon that absorb several hits
item.cardSummary: Inferno burns whoever hits you. It only matters if the user lives long enough to take those hits, so it is a tank placeholder, not a sweeper Trait.

item.name: Frenzy
item.effect: When hit, 11% chance to raise Attack by 3 stages
item.bestUse: Physical attackers that can survive a hit
item.cardSummary: Frenzy's +3 Attack swing is huge when it lands, but it waits for a hit and only has an 11% chance, so most fights end without it.

item.name: StoneHeart
item.effect: When hit, 11% chance to raise Defense by 3 stages
item.bestUse: Physical walls, and only as a filler roll
item.cardSummary: StoneHeart can harden Defense after a physical hit, but special attackers ignore it and the chance is low. Reroll it on any carry you plan to keep.

item.name: Venomward
item.effect: When hit, 33% chance to put 1 Poison stack on the attacker
item.bestUse: Tanks that want Poison without attacking
item.cardSummary: Venomward poisons the attacker when you get hit. It is a reactive filler Trait for walls, not a reason to stop rerolling a main attacker.

item.name: Frost
item.effect: On hit, 25% chance to put 1 Frostbite stack on the target
item.bestUse: Ice attackers that already hit every turn
item.cardSummary: Frost can add Frostbite from regular attacks. The 25% chance is lower than Sear or Toxin, so it is a weaker shared status roll.

item.name: Arcane
item.effect: When hit, 11% chance to raise Special Attack by 3 stages
item.bestUse: Special attackers that can take a hit
item.cardSummary: Arcane is Frenzy for special attackers. The +3 Special Attack boost is strong, but an 11% after-hit trigger is not a late-game plan.

item.name: Psywall
item.effect: When hit, 11% chance to raise Special Defense by 3 stages
item.bestUse: Special walls, and only as a filler roll
item.cardSummary: Psywall can raise Special Defense after a hit. Physical attackers skip the benefit, and the 11% chance makes it one of the weakest shared Traits.

item.name: Adapt
item.effect: Weather has no effect on this Evomon
item.bestUse: Teams that fight into Rain, Snow, Sandstorm, or Volcanic Eruption
item.cardSummary: Adapt ignores weather, which is a clean answer to weather damage and weather-boosted attacks. It does nothing if neither side is using weather.

item.name: SkyFire
item.effect: Below 50% HP, Fire-type skills gain 25% more power
item.bestUse: Fire attackers that can fight from half HP
item.cardSummary: SkyFire boosts Fire skills once the user is under half health. It is blank on non-Fire movesets and risky if the Evomon gets KO'd as soon as it crosses the threshold.

item.name: Dread
item.effect: On switch-in, lowers all foes' Special Attack by 2 stages
item.bestUse: Leads and tanks into special attackers
item.cardSummary: Dread drops every foe's Special Attack on entry. It is one of the best shared Traits into special teams and a dead slot against physical attackers.

item.name: Thorns
item.effect: When hit, reflects 12% of the damage taken
item.bestUse: Walls that expect repeated hits
item.cardSummary: Thorns sends 12% of incoming damage back at the attacker. It adds chip on bulky sets, but it rarely swings a fast KO race by itself.

item.name: Foresight
item.effect: Gains 12% critical-hit chance
item.bestUse: Attackers that already hit hard every turn
item.cardSummary: Foresight adds a flat 12% crit chance to every attack. It can steal KOs, but it is still luck-based compared with a always-on damage Trait.

item.name: Awe
item.effect: On first switch-in, lowers all foes' Attack by 2 stages
item.bestUse: Leads and tanks into physical attackers
item.cardSummary: Awe cuts every foe's Attack the first time you enter. Time the first switch, because special attackers ignore it and later re-entries do not retrigger it.

item.name: VitalGuard
item.effect: Cannot be hit by critical strikes
item.bestUse: Walls that need predictable bulk
item.cardSummary: VitalGuard blocks crits, which makes defensive math much safer. It does nothing against teams that are not leaning on critical hits.

item.name: Abyss
item.effect: Below 50% HP, Water-type skills gain 25% more power
item.bestUse: Water attackers that can fight from half HP
item.cardSummary: Abyss boosts Water skills under half health. Non-Water movesets get nothing, and a burst KO from above 50% HP skips the bonus entirely.

item.name: Toughskin
item.effect: Takes 12% less damage
item.bestUse: Any bulky Evomon
item.cardSummary: Toughskin is a simple 12% damage cut that stays on for the whole fight. It is one of the best shared Traits because almost every tank set can use it.

item.name: Renew
item.effect: Below 50% HP, Grass-type skills gain 25% more power
item.bestUse: Grass attackers that can fight from half HP
item.cardSummary: Renew boosts Grass skills under half health. It rewards bulky Grass attackers and is wasted on mixed or non-Grass movesets.

item.name: Blind
item.effect: Inflicting Psy Marks also applies 1 extra stack
item.bestUse: Psy Mark stacking teams
item.cardSummary: Blind doubles Psy Mark stacking speed on the Datunymph line. It is blank if the moveset is not built around Psy Marks.

item.name: Purify
item.effect: Cleanses 1 random debuff from itself at the end of each turn
item.bestUse: Status-heavy fights and long PvE
item.cardSummary: Purify peels one random debuff off Empixy-line Evomon every turn without spending an action. Stacked debuffs can still remove the least important one first.

item.name: Raincall
item.effect: On first switch-in, sets Rain for 5 turns
item.bestUse: Rain teams that need free weather setup
item.cardSummary: Raincall puts Rain up the first time the Clam line enters, which enables Rainveil and Water plans without a weather turn. The line has to be worth the team slot.

item.name: SoulShock
item.effect: When defeated, inflicts Confusion on the attacker for 2 turns
item.bestUse: Sacrifice leads that can punish the KO
item.cardSummary: SoulShock confuses the attacker after Mopillow falls. You have to lose the Evomon first, and Confusion does not always turn into a real opening.

item.name: Leech
item.effect: Restores HP equal to 66% of Poison damage dealt
item.bestUse: Poison attackers that stay in for several turns
item.cardSummary: Leech turns the Chitaldin line's Poison into healing. Cleanse, Poison resistance, or a target that falls too fast all cut the sustain.

item.name: Regen
item.effect: Restores 15% of max HP at the end of each turn while below 50% HP
item.bestUse: Bulky Grass walls
item.cardSummary: Regen pulls the Silvanarch line out of KO range as long as they stay under half HP. A burst from above 50% skips the heal window entirely.

item.name: Emberbirth
item.effect: Restores HP equal to 100% of Burn damage dealt
item.bestUse: Burn-focused Lavarock sets
item.cardSummary: Emberbirth is Lavarock's Burn lifesteal Trait. It heals for all Burn damage dealt, so it only pays off on sets that keep Burn active.

item.name: Flamefiend
item.effect: On switch-in, sets Volcanic Eruption weather for 5 turns
item.bestUse: Fire weather teams
item.cardSummary: Flamefiend starts Volcanic Eruption as soon as the Blazmane line enters. It can also overwrite weather another teammate needed, so the rest of the team has to want that weather.

item.name: UltGuard
item.effect: The first Ultimate Skill that hits this Evomon deals 50% less damage
item.bestUse: Boss fights and PvP into a known Ultimate
item.cardSummary: UltGuard halves the first Ultimate that hits the Pebgolem line. It is a one-use shield, so a weaker Ultimate can bait it before the real finisher.

item.name: Chillwind
item.effect: Inflicting Frostbite also applies 1 extra stack
item.bestUse: Frostbite stacking Frostseer sets
item.cardSummary: Chillwind makes Frostseer stack Frostbite twice as fast. It has no fallback if the opponent shuts down Frostbite.

item.name: OpenSupport
item.effect: Status skills gain +1 priority
item.bestUse: Support sets that spam status moves
item.cardSummary: OpenSupport lets Frostelle and Stardrift fire status skills with extra priority. Direct-damage builds get nothing from it.

item.name: BattleSpirit
item.effect: On first switch-in, raises Attack and Special Attack by 3 stages
item.bestUse: Astraknight sweepers that enter on their own terms
item.cardSummary: BattleSpirit gives Astraknight a free +3 to both attacking stats the first time it enters. A forced early switch wastes most of the Trait.

item.name: Reaper
item.effect: After defeating a target, raises Attack and Special Attack by 5 stages
item.bestUse: Sweepers that can secure the first KO
item.cardSummary: Reaper turns one KO into a +5/+5 snowball on the Leafblade line. If that first KO does not happen, the Trait never starts.

item.name: Pursuit
item.effect: Deals 18% more damage
item.bestUse: Any Sundercrene attacker that just wants more damage
item.cardSummary: Pursuit is a flat 18% damage increase on the Sundercrene line. It has no setup, weather, or HP condition, which makes it one of the most reliable offensive Traits.

item.name: PartingGift
item.effect: When defeated, restores 2 Energy
item.bestUse: Planned sacrifices that need a small Energy refund
item.cardSummary: PartingGift refunds 2 Energy after the Mudthorn line is KO'd. The refund only happens if you lose the Evomon, and two Energy is a small payoff.

item.name: Rainveil
item.effect: During Rain, Water-type skills gain +40 Power
item.bestUse: Rain Water attackers, usually next to Raincall
item.cardSummary: Rainveil is a large Water damage jump once Rain is up. The Bubble line still needs a Rain setter, or the Trait stays inactive.

item.name: Claws
item.effect: Inflicting Bleed also applies 1 extra stack
item.bestUse: Bleed stacking Chirphantom sets
item.cardSummary: Claws doubles Bleed stacks on the Chirphantom line. It only matters if the moveset actually inflicts Bleed.

item.name: Drain
item.effect: Gains 18% lifesteal
item.bestUse: Volcrest attackers in long fights
item.cardSummary: Drain gives Volcrest 18% lifesteal on damaging turns with no extra condition. It will not save a clean one-shot, but it is excellent sustain in longer battles.

item.name: Charge
item.effect: On first switch-in, damage dealt is doubled
item.bestUse: Arcapex openers that need a first-turn KO
item.cardSummary: Charge doubles Arcapex's first-entry damage. Bring it in when you can spend that burst; a wasted first switch throws the Trait away.

item.name: Perpetual
item.effect: After defeating a target, restores 2 PP to all skills
item.bestUse: Long PvE sessions on Tinkore
item.cardSummary: Perpetual refunds PP on the Tinkore line after each KO. Short fights and single-target bosses rarely care about PP, so it is a grinding Trait more than a PvP Trait.

item.name: Primeform
item.effect: Takes 60% less damage while at full HP
item.bestUse: Terragon walls that can stay at full HP
item.cardSummary: Primeform makes Terragon very hard to burst from full health. Any chip, weather, or damage-over-time turns the 60% cut off.

item.name: Evolve
item.effect: Applying Poison also inflicts 2 stacks of Psy Mark
item.bestUse: Wisphex Poison plus Psy Mark sets
item.cardSummary: Evolve lets the Wisphex line apply Poison and two Psy Marks with the same action. It is locked to that status plan, but the payoff is strong enough to build around.

item.name: TrueDmg
item.effect: Ignores the target's Defense and Special Defense stat stages
item.bestUse: Pummash into setup walls
item.cardSummary: TrueDmg lets Pummash punch through Defense and Special Defense boosts. Unboosted targets give it no extra value.

item.name: Infect
item.effect: Inflicting Poison also applies 1 extra stack
item.bestUse: Viparch Poison attackers
item.cardSummary: Infect doubles Poison stacking on the Viparch line. Cleanses and Poison-resistant targets erase most of the benefit.

item.name: Sandgale
item.effect: During Sandstorm, Ground-type and Rock-type skills gain +40 Power
item.bestUse: Sandstorm Ground and Rock attackers
item.cardSummary: Sandgale is a large Ground and Rock damage jump once Sandstorm is up. Without weather support, the Trait stays off.

item.name: SandFiend
item.effect: On first switch-in, sets Sandstorm for 5 turns
item.bestUse: Sandstorm teams, often next to Sandgale
item.cardSummary: SandFiend puts Sandstorm up the first time Spikumane enters, which enables Sandgale without a weather turn. Later re-entries do not retrigger it.

item.name: SnowFiend
item.effect: On first switch-in, sets Snow for 5 turns
item.bestUse: Snow and Ice weather teams
item.cardSummary: SnowFiend starts Snow the first time the Glacitadel line enters. The rest of the team still has to turn that weather into pressure.

item.name: Unseen
item.effect: When attacking a target with stat boosts, steals 2 random stat stages
item.bestUse: Gempress into setup users
item.cardSummary: Unseen steals two random boosted stages from a setup target. It does nothing to unboosted foes, and the stolen stats are not always the ones you want.

item.name: Blight
item.effect: Transfers negative stat stages from foes to their replacement on switch
item.bestUse: PvP against switch-heavy teams
item.cardSummary: Blight keeps stat drops stuck to the next Evomon when the opponent switches. Bosses and most PvE enemies rarely switch, so a lot of its value is PvP-only.

item.name: Deathrattle
item.effect: When defeated, deals 33% of the attacker's max HP as damage, up to 300
item.bestUse: Sacrifice leads that can finish a weakened attacker
item.cardSummary: Deathrattle punishes the KO on the Mirefish line. The 300-damage cap is weak into high-HP bosses, and you still have to lose the Evomon to use it.
